thread:
Emily Tran: FYI I opened a small PR consolidating Dedicated provisioning guidance: migration checklist (reserved -> dedicated), a compact autoscale YAML, and an SDK snippet for tenant labeling. PR: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/4820. Please review SLA wording and cooldown default.

Raj Patel: Quick note: avoid saying "best-effort" alone. Suggest: 'Dedicated capacity is covered by SLA-backed latency targets; fallback tiers (burst/shared) are not SLA-backed and can be preempted for maintenance or capacity constraints.' Add a one-liner about maintenance preemption windows.

Sam Kim: YAML nit: include explicit tenant labels so users see how to opt in. Example: `labels:\n  tenant_label: "team-alpha"\n  isolation: "tenant"` under allocation.

Claire Jones: Found a stale handbook anchor in the migration checklist; should point to `#capacity-modes`. I can push a tiny commit to fix.

Marc Brown: SDK snippet to drop into "Programmatic provisioning":
```python
from redwood import DedicatedClient
client = DedicatedClient(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
cap = client.create_capacity(name="team-alpha-dedicated", region="us-east-1", scale_policy={"min_replicas":2,"max_replicas":6,"cooldown_seconds":300}, labels={"tenant_label":"team-alpha","isolation":"tenant"})
print(cap)
```

Marc Brown: Add short note: runtime may preempt for infra maintenance; surface under SLA/evictions.

Liz Yang: Strong +1 for cooldown=300s. Our sims show 60s oscillates. Recommend adding a brief test plan: 1) spike->scale-up observed, 2) sustained load->stability, 3) cooldown->delayed scale-down, 4) eviction->fallback behavior.

docs-bot: Lint: docs/lint passed. Link-check: 1 anchor flagged -> Claire fixed.

Emily Tran: Thanks all. Claire please push the anchor fix. I'll update the SDK snippet, set cooldown default to 300, add Raj's SLA phrasing and the test plan, then send SLA sentence to legal. Will merge after CI and legal thumbs.
